mainTopic: מי שפרע: informing or cursing, and how much a down payment (ערבון) acquires
overview: This amud opens by answering a difficulty against ריש לקיש: the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון. Then the גמרא turns to the משנה's warning of מי שפרע, said to someone who backs out of a deal after the money was paid. אביי says we only inform him of the punishment, and רבא says we actually curse him, and each brings a פסוק. רבא tries to prove his view from a story where רבי יוחנן told רבי חייא בר יוסף to deliver salt or accept מי שפרע. The גמרא rejects the proof and retells the story as a question about a down payment (ערבון). That leads to a disagreement: רב says a down payment acquires only its own value, while רבי יוחנן says it acquires the whole deal. A ברייתא seems to challenge רב, but the גמרא answers that land, which money truly acquires, is different from movable items. Finally, the גמרא suggests that the dispute matches a תנאים argument about collateral and שמיטה, and it begins testing what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל meant. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to contradict ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא it just discussed is a problem for ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then this is difficult for ריש לקיש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge: the ברייתא just quoted does not seem to fit the view of ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן disagreed about what makes a sale final according to the Torah. The ברייתא that was just explained fits רבי יוחנן smoothly, so the question now is how ריש לקיש can live with it.

phrases.english: But it is difficult for Reish Lakish!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש from before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view on how a sale becomes final
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא appears to follow רבי יוחנן's approach, so it seems to go against ריש לקיש.

steps.title: ריש לקיש says the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that the ברייתא follows the view of רבי שמעון, so it does not bind him.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש could say to you: Whose view is this? It is רבי שמעון's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for ריש לקיש: the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, not the חכמים whose view ריש לקיש follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not change the ברייתא at all. It only says which תנא taught it. Since ריש לקיש can side with a different תנא, the ברייתא is no longer a problem for him.
steps.whatToRemember: When a ברייתא goes against an אמורא, the גמרא can answer that it follows one תנא, and the אמורא follows another.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish could say to you:
Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Shimon's.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: הָא מַנִּי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is a general rule that ריש לקיש must accept.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, and ריש לקיש can follow the other view.

steps.title: אביי and רבא disagree about מי שפרע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about מי שפרע and brings a disagreement: אביי says we inform the person, רבא says we curse him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'But they said: He Who exacted payment...' It was stated: אביי said, we inform him. רבא said, we curse him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה's warning of מי שפרע and brings a disagreement about how it is used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if someone backs out of a deal after the money was paid, God Who punished earlier generations will punish him too. אביי holds the court only tells him this warning. רבא holds the court actually says it to him as a curse.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He Who exacted payment' — the warning against backing out of a deal

steps.confusionAlert: Both agree the person hears the words of מי שפרע. The question is only whether it is said as information or as a real curse.

phrases.english: But they said: He Who exacted payment, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה continues: from the generation of the flood and the dispersion, He will punish whoever does not keep his word.

phrases.english: It was stated: Abaye said:
We inform him.
Rava said: We curse him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: the court informs the person of the warning. רבא: the court curses him with it.

steps.title: The פסוקים behind each view
steps.stepSummary: אביי uses the פסוק forbidding cursing a fellow Jew. רבא reads 'among your people' to mean only someone who acts properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said we inform him, because it says 'Do not curse a leader among your people.' רבא said we curse him, because 'among your people' means one who acts like your people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where each view comes from in the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי says cursing any Jew is forbidden by the פסוק, so the court may only inform. רבא focuses on the word 'בעמך': the ban protects only someone who acts the way the Jewish people should. A person who backs out after being paid is not acting that way, so he may be cursed.

keyTerms.meaning: one who acts the way your people should

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common idea: some Torah protections apply only to a Jew who acts properly.

phrases.english: Abaye said: We inform him,
as it is written: 'Nor curse a leader among your people.'
Rava said: We curse him,
as it is written: 'Among your people' —
with one who acts the way your people act.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אוֹדוֹעֵי מוֹדְעִינַן לֵיהּ, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the Torah source for each side of step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי relies on the ban against cursing. רבא limits that ban to someone acting properly.

steps.title: רבא's proof from רבי חייא בר יוסף and the salt
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a story: רבי יוחנן told רבי חייא בר יוסף to deliver the salt or accept מי שפרע. Since רבי חייא already knew the law, it must be a curse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: How do I know this? People gave רבי חייא בר יוסף money for salt. Then salt went up in price. He came to רבי יוחנן, who told him: Go give it to them, and if not, accept מי שפרע. If it were only informing, does רבי חייא בר יוסף need to be informed?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tries to prove his view from a real story with רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא בר יוסף was a great scholar and already knew about מי שפרע. So telling him 'accept מי שפרע' could not just be giving him information. רבא concludes it must be a real curse.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do I say this?
someone who needs to be informed

phrases.english: Rava said: From where do I say this?
For Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Yosef —
they gave him money for salt.
In the end, salt went up in price.
He came before Rabbi Yoḥanan,
who said to him: Go give it to them,
and if not — accept upon yourself 'He Who exacted payment.'
And if you say we only inform him,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף בַּר אוֹדוֹעֵי הוּא.
phrases.english: is Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Yosef someone who needs to be informed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's side of the disagreement.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that the court curses the person with מי שפרע
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי יוחנן telling רבי חייא בר יוסף to accept מי שפרע

steps.title: The story does not prove a curse either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: would רבי חייא בר יוסף ever accept a curse of the חכמים? So the story proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what? That we curse him? Would רבי חייא בר יוסף come to accept a curse of the חכמים upon himself?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רבא's proof by showing his own reading of the story has the same problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'accept מי שפרע' meant a real curse, it is just as hard to imagine that a great scholar would agree to be cursed by the חכמים. Since the story is strange for both views, it cannot prove רבא right over אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, what? (turns the question back on the other side)

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's proof is rejected. The story fits poorly with both views, so the disagreement between אביי and רבא stays open here.

phrases.english: Rather, what — that we curse him?
Would Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Yosef come
to accept upon himself a curse of the Sages?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof, not רבא's view itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The story is just as hard to explain under רבא's view, so it cannot decide between the two views.

steps.title: The story was really about a down payment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-explains the story: רבי חייא בר יוסף had received a down payment. He thought it acquired only its own value, and רבי יוחנן told him it acquires the whole deal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the buyers gave רבי חייא בר יוסף a down payment. He thought it bought only as much as it was worth. רבי יוחנן told him it buys the whole deal.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting רבא's proof, the גמרא offers a new way to understand the story of רבי חייא בר יוסף and the salt. He did know the law of מי שפרע. The real question was how much a down payment acquires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא assumed רבי חייא already knew everything, so רבי יוחנן's words had to be a curse. Now the גמרא shows something he did not know: whether a down payment covers the whole sale. So רבי יוחנן was teaching him a law, and the story no longer proves רבא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: A down payment, a part of the price paid up front
It acquires only as much as it is worth

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Chiyya bar Yosef:
phrases.notes: This goes back to the salt story from step 5. The גמרא now tells it in a new way.

phrases.english: it was a down payment that they gave him.
He held: it acquires only as much as it is worth.
And Rabbi Yochanan said to him:
It acquires the whole amount of the deal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף עֵרָבוֹן הוּא דְּיָהֲבִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the דחיה, the גמרא gives the story a new reading so that it no longer supports רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case behind the story
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חייא knew the law, so רבי יוחנן's words must have been a curse.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי חייא did not know how much a down payment acquires. רבי יוחנן was teaching him that it acquires the whole deal.

steps.title: רב and רבי יוחנן disagree about down payments
steps.stepSummary: A recorded disagreement: רב says a down payment acquires only its own value. רבי יוחנן says it acquires the whole deal.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated about a down payment: רב says it acquires only what it is worth. רבי יוחנן says it acquires the whole deal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a formal disagreement between אמוראים on the question raised in the story. רב and רבי יוחנן split on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's view matches what he told רבי חייא בר יוסף. רב holds the opposite, the same view רבי חייא had. This sets up a challenge against רב.

phrases.english: It was stated about a down payment:
Rav says: it acquires only as much as it is worth;

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: כְּנֶגֶד כּוּלּוֹ הוּא קוֹנֶה.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yochanan said: it acquires the whole amount of the deal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the down-payment question from the story and presents it as a full disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: a down payment acquires only its own value. רבי יוחנן: it acquires the entire sale.

steps.title: A ברייתא about penalty conditions on a down payment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a challenge by quoting a ברייתא. Buyer and seller each set a penalty for backing out, and רבי יוסי says the conditions hold.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: if someone gives a down payment and says, 'If I back out, you keep my down payment,' and the other says, 'If I back out, I will pay you double,' the conditions hold. This is the view of רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge against רב by quoting a ברייתא. This first part is setup. The actual question comes later in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This part of the ברייתא is about penalty conditions, not yet about how much the down payment acquires. The גמרא quotes the whole source because the key line, from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, comes further on.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: One who gives a down payment to another,
and says to him: 'If I back out,
my down payment is forfeited to you,'

phrases.aramaic: וְהַלָּה אוֹמֵר לוֹ: ״אִם אֲנִי אֶחְזוֹר בִּי,
phrases.english: and the other one says to him: 'If I back out,
I will pay you back double your down payment,'
the conditions take effect. These are the words of Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts quoting a ברייתא in order to challenge רב's view from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that a down payment acquires only its own value
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only. The point of the attack shows up in the later lines of the same ברייתא.

steps.title: רבי יוסי follows his usual view on אסמכתא
steps.stepSummary: A side comment from the גמרא: רבי יוסי rules this way because he holds that אסמכתא still acquires.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי follows his own reasoning, since he says an אסמכתא does acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses for a short side comment. It explains why רבי יוסי lets these penalty conditions stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side made a promise expecting never to have to pay it. That kind of promise is called אסמכתא. רבי יוסי holds that it still binds, which explains his ruling. This is a side point, not the main challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: A promise made expecting never to have to carry it out

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei follows his own reasoning,
since he says: an אסמכתא does acquire.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּאָמַר: אַסְמַכְתָּא קָנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side note explaining רבי יוסי's ruling in the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי holds that an אסמכתא acquires, so the penalty conditions take effect.

steps.title: רבי יהודה and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל on how much is acquired
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. רבי יהודה says the down payment acquires only its own value. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל limits that to when the buyer said 'let my down payment acquire.' With a house or field, partial payment acquires the whole thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: it is enough that the down payment acquires as much as it is worth. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: when is this true? When he said, 'Let my down payment acquire.' But if he sold a house or field for 1,000 זוז and was paid 500, the buyer acquires all of it. He pays the rest even years later.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the ברייתא. This part deals with exactly our question: how much a down payment acquires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה sounds like רב. But רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that ruling applies only when the buyer clearly said his down payment should acquire only its share. In a regular sale of land, half the payment acquires the whole property. This sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It is enough for it, only this much
When is this said? Limits a ruling to a certain case

steps.confusionAlert: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does not argue with רבי יהודה's rule itself. He narrows it to one case, when the buyer said 'let my down payment acquire.'

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: דַּיּוֹ שֶׁיִּקְנֶה כְּנֶגֶד עֵרְבוֹנוֹ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: it is enough that it acquires as much as his down payment is worth.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
When is this said?
When he said to him, 'Let my down payment acquire.'

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מָכַר לוֹ בַּיִת אוֹ שָׂדֶה בְּאֶלֶף זוּז,
phrases.english: But if he sold him a house or a field for a thousand זוז,

phrases.aramaic: וּפָרַע לוֹ מֵהֶם חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת זוּז – קָנָה,
phrases.english: and the buyer paid him five hundred זוז of it, he has acquired it all,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַחֲזִיר לוֹ אֶת הַשְּׁאָר אֲפִילּוּ לְאַחַר כַּמָּה שָׁנִים.
phrases.english: and he pays him the rest, even after several years.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: דַּיּוֹ שֶׁיִּקְנֶה כְּנֶגֶד עֵרְבוֹנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 9 and reaches the part that matters for the challenge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: a down payment acquires only its value. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: only when the buyer said so. In a land sale, partial payment acquires everything.

steps.title: Does the same apply to movable items, against רב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: doesn't the same rule apply to movable items? Then an unspecified down payment acquires the whole deal, against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't the same true for movable items? When nothing was spelled out, the buyer acquires all of it!
steps.whatsHappening: Here the challenge against רב lands. The גמרא suggests that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's rule for land also covers movable items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a plain, unspecified down payment acquires the whole deal even for movable items, that matches רבי יוחנן. It goes against רב, who said it acquires only its own value. The question is phrased 'isn't it so...?', which leaves room for an answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it so that...? Suggests a reading of a source
Unspecified, when nothing was spelled out

steps.whatToRemember: רב says a down payment acquires only its own value. רבי יוחנן says it acquires the whole deal. The ברייתא, through רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, seems to support רבי יוחנן and so challenges רב. Steps 13 and 14 answer this challenge.

phrases.english: Is it not that the same law applies to movable items,
that when nothing was spelled out, he acquires all of them!
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is in the printed גמרא. The word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean the same here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's rule from step 11 and uses it against רב from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that a down payment acquires only its own value
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the land rule also covers movable items, an unspecified down payment acquires the whole sale. That matches רבי יוחנן and contradicts רב.

steps.title: Movable items are different: an unspecified down payment does not acquire everything
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. With movable items, an unspecified down payment does not acquire the whole item.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. With movable items, when nothing was specified, the buyer does not acquire the whole thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 12 by saying 'No.' רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's rule about land does not carry over to movable items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 assumed that if partial payment acquires a whole field, it must also acquire a whole movable item. The גמרא says this does not follow. For movable items, an unspecified down payment does not acquire the whole thing, so רב's view still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Movable items, anything you can pick up and carry, as opposed to land
In an unspecified case, where nobody said exactly what the payment covers

phrases.english: No, movable items in an unspecified case are not acquired (in full).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 12 by denying that the land rule applies to movable items.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases (land and movable items follow different rules)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since partial payment acquires a whole field, it should also acquire a whole movable item, which would go against רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: For movable items, an unspecified down payment acquires only its own value, so רב is not contradicted.

steps.title: Why land and movable items are different
steps.stepSummary: Money truly acquires land, so a down payment acquires the whole field. Money only makes movable items subject to the curse of 'מי שפרע,' so it does not acquire the whole item.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why is land different? Land is truly acquired with money, so the down payment acquires all of it. Movable items are not truly acquired with money. Paying only means that a person who backs out has to accept the curse 'He Who exacted payment.' So the payment does not acquire the whole item.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why land and movable items should be treated differently, and then gives the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For land, money is a real way of acquiring, so even part of the money can acquire the whole field. For movable items, money is not a real way of acquiring. It only means that someone who backs out gets the curse of 'מי שפרע.' A weak tool like that cannot stretch past the amount actually paid.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is the difference? A question asking why two cases are treated differently
'He Who exacted payment.' The curse said to someone who backs out of a deal after money was paid

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how רב can accept רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's rule about land and still hold that a down payment on movable items acquires only its own value.

phrases.english: And what is different about land?
With money, one truly acquires it,
so he acquires all of it.
Movable items, which (money) acquires only
to make (a person who backs out) accept 'He Who exacted payment,'
phrases.notes: This is the curse said to someone who backs out after money was paid. With movable items, that is all the money accomplishes.

phrases.english: he does not acquire all of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the distinction made in Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the reason behind the distinction
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Land and movable items should behave the same way when a down payment is made.
steps.terutzMaskana: Money truly acquires land, so partial payment covers all of it. For movable items, money only brings the curse of 'מי שפרע,' so partial payment covers only its own value.

steps.title: Suggesting a parallel in a תנאים dispute: collateral and שמיטה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the argument between רב and רבי יוחנן matches a ברייתא. There, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that שמיטה does not cancel a loan with collateral even if the collateral is worth only half the loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is like a dispute between תנאים. If someone lends money to his friend and takes collateral, and then שמיטה arrives, the loan is not canceled even if the collateral is worth only half. These are the words of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes that the argument between רב and רבי יוחנן is really an older argument between תנאים. It begins quoting a ברייתא about collateral and שמיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Collateral is being compared to a down payment: a small item that secures a bigger obligation. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says collateral worth only half still protects the loan from שמיטה. That sounds like רבי יוחנן's view that a partial payment covers the whole deal.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say it is like a dispute between תנאים. The גמרא suggests that an argument between אמוראים matches an earlier one
Collateral, an item the lender holds as security for a loan
The seventh year, when loans are canceled

phrases.english: Let us say it is like a dispute between תנאים:
One who lends to his friend on collateral,
and the שמיטה year arrived,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ שָׁוֶה אֶלָּא פְּלָג –
phrases.english: even though it (the collateral) is worth only half (the loan),
(שמיטה) does not cancel (the loan),
these are the words of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רב has been defended, the גמרא opens a new line by looking for a תנאים source behind the dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: a loan secured by collateral is not canceled by שמיטה, even if the collateral is worth only half the loan.

steps.title: רבי יהודה הנשיא: protection only when the collateral matches the loan
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה הנשיא says that שמיטה does not cancel the loan only if the collateral is worth the full loan. Otherwise it does cancel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה הנשיא says: If the collateral was worth as much as his loan, שמיטה does not cancel it. If not, שמיטה cancels it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the other side of the argument, the view of רבי יהודה הנשיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה הנשיא seems to require collateral equal to the loan before it protects the loan. At first glance, that looks like רב's view that a partial payment covers only its own value.

keyTerms.meaning: Equal to the amount of his loan

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה הנשיא here is a different person from the רבי יהודה quoted in Step 11, and this is a different ברייתא. Don't mix the two up.

phrases.english: רבי יהודה הנשיא says:
If the collateral was equal to his loan,
(שמיטה) does not cancel (it),
and if not, it cancels (it).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in Step 15 with the opposing view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה הנשיא: שמיטה does not cancel the loan only when the collateral equals the loan. Otherwise שמיטה cancels it.

steps.title: What does רבן שמעון בן גמליאל mean by 'does not cancel'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly רבן שמעון בן גמליאל means when he says שמיטה 'does not cancel.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'does not cancel' mean, as רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling actually means. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא tests a possible reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested parallel only works if we know how far the collateral's protection goes. Does it protect only the half it is worth, or the whole loan? The גמרא will test each option.

keyTerms.meaning: That he said, referring back to someone's words

phrases.english: What is 'does not cancel'
that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אֵינוֹ מְשַׁמֵּט דְּקָאָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact meaning of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling from Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'does not cancel' means that only the part equal to the collateral is protected, or that the whole loan is protected.

steps.title: Testing the first reading: only the matching half is protected
steps.stepSummary: Suppose רבן שמעון בן גמליאל means that only the half matching the collateral is protected. Then רבי יהודה הנשיא would hold that even that half is canceled, which makes no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means only the part equal to the collateral is protected, then it follows that רבי יהודה הנשיא holds that even that half is canceled!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first reading of 'does not cancel' and shows that it leads to a strange result for רבי יהודה הנשיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבן שמעון בן גמליאל protects only the half covered by the collateral, then רבי יהודה הנשיא, who disagrees, must hold that even that covered half is canceled. But the lender is holding collateral worth that half. It is hard to believe that שמיטה would cancel it, so this reading looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say. Introduces a possible reading that the גמרא is about to test
From this it follows. Introduces what must be true if the reading is correct

phrases.english: If you say (it means only the part) equal to it,
phrases.notes: Meaning only the part of the loan matching what the collateral is worth stays protected.

phrases.english: it follows that רבי יהודה הנשיא holds:
even that half is canceled too!
phrases.notes: The exclamation is the problem: the collateral fully covers that half, so how could it be canceled?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא כְּנֶגְדּוֹ, מִכְּלָל דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַנָּשִׂיא סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the question in Step 17 and attacks it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל protects only the part of the loan equal to the collateral.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under this reading, the opposing view of רבי יהודה הנשיא would have to cancel even the half that the collateral fully covers. That result is unreasonable, so the reading is called into doubt.
